competitor_alerts: NEW COMPETITOR: Shi-Ya, a 100% kosher sushi restaurant from the owners of Meat Point, opened June 2026 and earned coverage in the Dallas Observer's new-openings roundup (https://www.dallasobserver.com/food-drink/new-dallas-restaurants-opened-june-2026-40693920/). Meat Point is actively expanding its kosher footprint and press presence.

Simcha Kosher Catering and A Taste of the World outrank us on both 'kosher catering Dallas' and 'Jewish catering Dallas'. Both run dedicated catering-focused websites with address markup and review counts; we appear but lower on the page.

dallaskosher.org is the authority directory ranking #1-2 for nearly every target keyword (food, restaurant, catering, delivery, Shabbat). The Hungry Rooster is not listed in its Restaurants or Catering directories — a major visibility gap on the exact pages our customers browse.

Delivery-intent keywords ('kosher delivery Dallas', 'kosher meal delivery Texas') are fully owned by aggregators (Uber Eats, DoorDash, Postmates, Shef). We are not present on these marketplaces' Dallas kosher category pages, so we capture none of that high-intent delivery traffic.

recommendations.action: Fix the canonical tags. Every subpage (/menu, /catering, /shabbat) currently sets <link rel=canonical> to the homepage root (https://thehungryroostertx.com). Give each page a self-referencing canonical URL.
recommendations.reason: A homepage-pointing canonical tells Google not to index the subpages on their own. This is the most likely technical reason our /catering page does not rank for 'kosher catering Dallas' despite having relevant content — Google is being told the catering page is a duplicate of the homepage.

recommendations.action: Get The Hungry Rooster listed on dallaskosher.org's Restaurants and Catering directory pages (and confirm current Dallas VAAD / kosher-certification listing).
recommendations.reason: dallaskosher.org ranks #1-2 for almost every one of our target keywords and we are absent from it. Being listed there is the fastest way to appear on page 1 for 'kosher food Dallas', 'kosher restaurant Dallas', and 'Shabbat meals Dallas' via a trusted authority site.

recommendations.action: Server-render the Shabbat page. /shabbat currently returns only 'Loading this week's Shabbat menu...' with the actual menu injected client-side; give it real crawlable HTML plus a heading like 'Kosher Shabbat Meals & Dinner Delivery in Dallas'.
recommendations.reason: 'Shabbat meals Dallas' is a target keyword and we don't rank. Google largely sees an empty page because the content is JS-loaded, so there is nothing to index for our single most on-brand keyword.

recommendations.action: Claim/optimize marketplace listings on Uber Eats, DoorDash, and Postmates under the Dallas 'kosher' category, and add a dedicated 'Delivery' page targeting 'kosher delivery Dallas'.
recommendations.reason: Every delivery-intent keyword is owned by these aggregators and we appear on none of their kosher category pages. This is high-purchase-intent traffic (people ready to order now) that currently goes entirely to competitors.

recommendations.action: Add LocalBusiness / Restaurant JSON-LD structured data (name, address 1499 Regal Row Suite 206, phone 945-215-7907, hours Mon-Fri 9am-2pm, geo, priceRange, servesCuisine: Kosher, sameAs social links). Could not confirm any JSON-LD in the current markup — verify and add if missing.
recommendations.reason: Structured data powers rich results and Google Business/Maps eligibility. Competitors like Meat Point and Aderet surface with rich listings; without it we forfeit map-pack and knowledge-panel visibility for local kosher searches.

recommendations.action: Build a dedicated, indexable reviews/testimonials page. The site only has a 'Leave a Review' link (/review); there is no public /reviews page showing social proof, and the /reviews path does not exist in navigation.
recommendations.reason: Top competitors show visible review counts (Simcha, A Taste of the World). A crawlable reviews page adds fresh keyword-rich content and trust signals, and supports Review/AggregateRating schema for star rich-results.

recommendations.action: Publish a blog post targeting 'kosher Shabbat dinner delivery Dallas' and 'weekly kosher dinner drops Dallas' — long-tail terms with weak, non-specific results.
recommendations.reason: No competitor owns these exact phrases and they match our weekly dinner-drop and Shabbat offering exactly. Low competition plus high relevance makes this a realistic page-1 win that also reinforces the /shabbat and delivery keywords.

recommendations.action: Differentiate page titles and meta descriptions per page. /menu, /catering, and /shabbat all reuse the identical homepage title and meta description.
recommendations.reason: Duplicate titles/descriptions across pages weaken relevance signals and hurt click-through. Unique, keyword-targeted titles (e.g. 'Kosher Catering Dallas — Corporate, Weddings & Shiva | The Hungry Rooster') help each page rank for its own term.

quick_wins: Change the canonical tag on /menu, /catering and /shabbat to point to themselves instead of the homepage root.
Submit The Hungry Rooster to the dallaskosher.org Restaurants and Catering directories.
Give /shabbat and /catering unique <title> and meta descriptions instead of reusing the homepage's.
summary: The Hungry Rooster's on-page basics are solid (strong homepage title, meta description, keyword and Open Graph tags), and we now appear on page 1 for 'kosher catering Dallas' (~#10) and 'Jewish catering Dallas' (~#8), but we're absent from every other target keyword. Two fixable technical issues are holding us back: every subpage canonicalizes to the homepage, so Google won't rank /catering or /shabbat on their own, and the Shabbat page's content is JavaScript-loaded and effectively invisible to crawlers. The biggest external gaps are not being listed on the authority directory dallaskosher.org and having zero presence on delivery marketplaces — plus a new competitor, Shi-Ya kosher sushi from the Meat Point team, just opened and is gaining press.
